decisions.question: Which exported functions and classes does the facade offer?
decisions.why: none: a frontend facade offers its elements as Effect UI bindings, and the exported classes are those elements' constructors (Button, BaseButton, ...), which an app never calls; the UI generator reads elements, not exports, so no handles follow either

decisions.question: Which upstream failures become which tagged errors?
decisions.why: kept: Fluent exports no error classes and the facade wraps no calls that fail; the catch-all is unused by the UI generator

decisions.question: Which handles are provided as services (Context.Service with a layer)?
decisions.why: kept: a frontend facade offers no handles

decisions.question: Which mounts does the frontend facade offer?
decisions.why: <fluent-dialog> has no `open` property: it opens and closes through `show()` and `hide()` and fires `toggle` after either. DialogOpen applies the view's `open` through those methods (only when the native dialog is elsewhere) and sends `{ open }` on each `toggle`, so the Model follows a close by Escape or a click outside; it releases nothing, since the element is the view's

decisions.question: Does the facade offer <fluent-dropdown-option>?
decisions.why: the manifest is stale: upstream registers this element as <fluent-option> (dist/esm/option/, tagName `${prefix}-option`); no module defines <fluent-dropdown-option>, and the binding imported the package root, which defines nothing

decisions.question: Does the facade offer <fluent-text-area>?
decisions.why: the manifest is stale: upstream registers this element as <fluent-textarea> (dist/esm/textarea/, tagName `${prefix}-textarea`); no module defines <fluent-text-area>, and the binding imported the package root, which defines nothing

decisions.question: Does the binding offer the property fluent-dialog.emitToggle?
decisions.why: a method stored as an instance field (an arrow function upstream binds to its own events); setting it from a view would replace upstream's handler
